> **What you can defend when you leave.** Set how you and your tools will work while the stakes are still small, verify your first AI assistance, and close by declaring the question your evidence will answer.

## The milestone ahead {#checkpoint}

Your curiosity is committed; this studio owns the arc's other three beats. First the ledger and rules: every studio after this one asks you to delegate real work to AI and stand behind the result under your own name, and those rules cannot be improvised under deadline pressure. Then the first verified AI assistance: one delegation on your own problem, checked by a method outside the tool, logged as the pattern every later exchange follows. And then the close: with rules standing and assistance verified, you declare the formal research question, because a project is only defensible if its question fixes what would count as an answer. Every later milestone appends to the ledger opened here, the claims of Studio 9 trace to the words declared here, and your Studio 12 defense reads this agreement back to you.

This studio closes with **[Milestone 2: Your rules and your question](milestone02-govern-the-work.qmd)**, a short chapter of its own after the lessons. **What it asks you to produce.** Your working agreement (a responsibility statement, your working rules, your opened AI Research Ledger, your delegation map, and the red-flag screen of your chosen problem) and your question, formally declared: objective, units, outcomes and conditions, kind and reach, and a provisional claim boundary.

Milestone 3 holds the declared question up against what is already known, and it will usually send back a sharper version. The milestone chapter keeps the working details: the practice steps, the versioned record, and how the artifact is assessed.

## The lessons in this studio

Read them in order, working each lesson's **It is your turn** as you go. Each one builds a piece of Milestone 2; beside each lesson is the piece it hands you.

- [Lesson 2 — AI Is Your Arm, Not Your Brain](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part1-research-with-ai/01-ai-is-your-arm-not-your-brain.html): your opened AI Research Ledger with its first verified exchange, run on your own problem's key fact.
- [Lesson 3 — The Student as Research Director](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part1-research-with-ai/02-the-student-as-research-director.html): your delegation map: the road's tasks sorted into safe to delegate, delegate then verify, and never delegate.
- [Lesson 4 — Specify, Delegate, Interrogate, Inspect, Verify, Document, Defend](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part1-research-with-ai/03-specify-delegate-interrogate-inspect-verify-document-defend.html): one complete SDIIVDD run on a checkable claim, with the verification you ran and what it caught.
- [Lesson 5 — Research Responsibility and Intellectual Ownership](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part1-research-with-ai/04-research-responsibility-and-intellectual-ownership.html): your ownership statement, your never-delegate list, and a first draft of your AI-use disclosure.
- [Lesson 6 — Descriptive, Predictive, and Causal Questions](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part2-curiosity-to-design/06-descriptive-predictive-and-causal-questions.html): your lead question placed by kind and reach, double-barrels split, with its comparison world written out if the question is causal: the arc's fourth beat, closed.

When the last lesson closes, the milestone chapter is next. Nothing you write in a lesson is busywork: every piece above is on the milestone's checklist.
